recentItems.title: Hello, Kyrgyzstan
recentItems.description:
The Kyrgyz Republic lies in eastern Central Asia, covering nearly 200,000 square kilometers with a population of about 7.4 million people. China and Kyrgyzstan, connected by mountains and rivers, have a long history of friendly ties. In 2023, the two countries upgraded their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, pledging to build a community with a shared future defined by good-neighborliness, friendship and shared prosperity.

recentItems.title: From Rome to Hong Kong: A modern Silk Road journey
recentItems.description:
More than 750 years after Marco Polo traveled east along the Silk Road, two modern-day travelers have followed in his footsteps with a very different mode of transport. Economist Jeffrey Sachs and investor Patrick Zhong have completed a 43-day, 15,000-kilometer journey from Rome to Hong Kong in an electric vehicle. What did they learn from engaging directly with people across Europe and Asia? Can the spirit of exchange that once defined the Silk Road still offer lessons for relations between East and West? And can people-to-people engagement help rebuild trust in an increasingly divided world?
Guests in this episode of Dialogue are Jeffrey D. Sachs, professor and director of the Center for Sustainable Development at Columbia University, and Patrick Zhong, founding managing partner of M31 Capital.

recentItems.title: Expert: Glacier collapse in Nepal triggered mudslide that hit Gyirong Port
recentItems.description:
A glacier collapse in Nepal triggered a high-speed mudslide that traveled nearly 20 kilometers to Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region in just seven minutes, according to Guo Zhaocheng, a senior engineer at the China Aero Geophysical Survey and Remote Sensing Center for Natural Resources.

The source area was around 5,140 meters above sea level, while Gyirong Port sits at about 1,800 meters – a drop of nearly 3,300 meters over a distance of just 20 kilometers. The dramatic descent converted enormous potential energy into powerful kinetic energy, driving the flow downhill at an estimated average speed of around 50 meters per second.

recentItems.title: Inside the SCO Box: India's rocket ambition
recentItems.description:
Sometimes one small object can tell more about a country than a long list of achievements. In our project SCO: BEYOND THE BOX, participants choose a symbol that reveals their country's role, and what it's ready to share with others.

For India, that symbol is a rocket — an image of ambition, science, and the drive to turn bold ideas into working solutions.

But progress isn't just about a single country's achievements. It is about sharing experience, forging connections, and growing together. That's the vision India brings to the SCO.

And what object would you choose for your country?

recentItems.title: Waste Makes a Green Comeback in Kyrgyzstan
recentItems.description:
In Bishkek, capital of Kyrgyzstan, household waste is being transformed into green electricity, with even the slag and steam produced during the process being put to good use. The project is a fruit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization countries' joint efforts to balance economic growth with environmental protection. The SCO is also expanding environmental cooperation and promoting greener awareness through education.

recentItems.title: Behind the China-Nepal mudslide: What caused its devastating force?
recentItems.description:
The China-Nepal border mudslide has caused heavy casualties and left many people missing on both sides. What triggered the disaster, and what made its destructive force so immense?
"This event was initially caused by a very large ice rock avalanche." Fan Xuanmei, a geohazard expert from Chengdu University of Technology, explains the factors behind the disaster and the extraordinary energy released by the mudslide.
